name: gods-eye-view
use_label: Live satellite globe in your browser
one_liner: Puts real satellite and flight tracks on a 3D globe in your browser.

text.why: Watching satellites or aircraft move normally means installing specialist software and wiring up a data source yourself. gods-eye-view moves that into a single browser screen, laying live open data over a photorealistic 3D globe. You install it with Pinokio or run it locally from the terminal and it opens in your own browser; it is built on Cesium. No license is declared in the repository, so check that before reusing the code.
text.take: The point is that a control-room view like this runs on your own machine from public data alone.
build: An internal briefing screen showing live open satellite data
A live observation demo page for a geography or space class

who.situation: shows live flights, satellites and quakes in class
wants to put open geodata on a 3D globe
views public signals in one place without paid tools

caveat: Photorealistic 3D and voice control need Cesium ion, Google or OpenAI keys
Data may be delayed or modelled; the README rules out navigation or emergency use
GitHub metadata shows no license, but the README states MIT

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: A frame from the README GIF: a 3D globe seen from orbit, overlaid with tracked-object labels and an orbit line.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
